Same subdued studio lighting from upper left, flat very light cool-grey background #F3F5F7 with faint soft contact shadow, restrained premium 3D educational rendering. Exercise: BARBELL BENT-OVER ROW, top position. Standing feet hip width, knees softly bent, hips hinged, torso about 35 degrees above horizontal, spine/neck neutral, eyes toward floor ahead. One straight bar with matching modest graphite plates and collars. Closed shoulder-width OVERHAND grips, elbows bent and traveling behind torso, bar gently near lower ribs/upper abdomen and NEVER through body. Wrists straight, forearms under bar, feet planted. Rear-side three-quarter camera shows back plane and near hand-bar contact, full bar and both feet. Coral broad latissimus dorsi and mid-back muscle regions only; spine itself, shoulders, arms grey.

revisions.reason: Torso too upright to communicate bent-over row
revisions.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit/scientific-educational. Image 1 is current barbell row EDIT TARGET; image 2 canonical model. Correct pose only: HINGE FORWARD MUCH MORE AT HIPS so torso is approximately 25-35 degrees ABOVE HORIZONTAL, almost parallel to floor. Push hips backward, flex knees moderately, maintain straight neutral back/neck; face looks down toward floor ahead rather than forward. Preserve top of row: same bar in FRONT of body at LOWER RIBS, not behind hips; both hands closed overhand, elbows bent pointing back past torso. Use more side-on rear three-quarter camera so hip hinge and front-of-body bar position are unambiguous. Keep identical character, charcoal shorts/shoes, coral back/lats overlay, continuous barbell/plates, planted feet, lighting and backdrop. No extra equipment.

review.notes: Revised hip hinge visibly deeper; bent elbows pull continuous bar close in front of lower torso, both feet planted, back/lats coral. Rear view partly occludes far grip and bar contact.
review.independentNotes: Viewed corrected image: moderate forward hinge, soft knees, elbows behind torso and bar drawn toward lower abdomen. Far hand is partly occluded.
